newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen cabinet starts discussing 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Yemen cabinet starts discussing 1997 budget.

text.p: Yemen's cabinet on Wednesday started discussions on its 1997 budget, with initial estimates pointing to a lower deficit, the official Saba news agency reported.

But political sources said the session was disrupted when ministers from the Islamist Islah party -- a partner in the coalition government -- walked out in protest over proposals to merge the curricula of religious institutes and other schools.
Saba said the cabinet "started today the discussion of the estimations of the general budget of the state for the year 1997".
The news agency put spending estimates for 1997 at 313 billion rials ($3.13 billion), and revenues at 301 billion rials -- giving an estimated forecast deficit of 12 billion rials.
This compares with forecast spending of 181.41 billion rials and income of 155.88 billion rials this year, which would give a 25.53 billion deficit.
Yemen suffers from high inflation estimated at 71 percent in 1995, but seen slowing to some 12 percent this year.
A political source told Reuters that ministers from the Islamist Islah party withdrew from the session.

"The withdrawal came in protest against the discussion of a proposed resolution to cancel the religious institutes in the country" and merge the curriculum with that of other educational institutions, the source said.
The party, headed by parliament speaker Sheikh Abdullah al-Ahmar, controls the institutes where a religious curriculum is followed. It allocates a special budget for these schools.
This week Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh called on the government to close down the religious institutes and unify the two curricula.
Saba said the cabinet would convene an extraordinary session on Thursday to complete discussion on the budget.
If approved, the budget will be referred to the parliament for endorsement. The president must then give final approval.
